assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have opened new measurement regimes: relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a path to redefining the second. The idea is original, the measurable performance is unambiguous, and it enables further work across physics. This is the kind of new measurement technique that expands what can be observed.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the decisive proposal and first realization of the lattice clock concept. Ye's group drove the performance to the current record and the many-body clock work. Only these two names are credited, which gives a clean two-person prize. Related contributions to the frequency comb and single-ion clocks were already recognized in 2005 and 2012, and that history needs to be handled carefully.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others) have confirmed the performance, including remote clock comparisons. The field is mature, and recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
I have not independently verified the exact record uncertainties and rely on recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, single-site imaging with quantum gas microscopes, and Hubbard-model studies, gave experimentalists a controllable platform for many-body physics. The experiments are careful and reproducible, and the platform has influenced condensed matter, quantum information and metrology. The consequences for other fields have been broad.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal supplied the theoretical basis, while Bloch's group performed the Mott transition experiment and much of the later development. Greiner led the quantum gas microscope work. Five credited names exceed the three-person limit, so I propose one theorist and two experimentalists. Dalibard and Cirac are credible alternatives and the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: The field is well established and replicated, and 2001 BEC prize and 2012 prize for quantum systems control give context. Quantum simulation as a goal is still maturing, but the underlying techniques are stable.
uncertainties: Choice among five credited names is arguable, especially Cirac versus Zoller and the role of Dalibard.
Overlap with the trapped-ion and Rydberg-array candidates in theoretical credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry is a precision measurement method with real use in gravimetry, gradiometry, tests of the equivalence principle and measurements of the fine-structure constant and G. It fits my view that progress is limited by how precisely we can measure. Light-pulse interferometers are demonstrated instruments, and applications such as mineral exploration and navigation are emerging.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard produced the first atom interferometers with material gratings and the early demonstrations. Kasevich and Chu produced the light-pulse interferometer and the high-precision gravimeters and gradiometers. Bordé contributed the theory and the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer. Steven Chu is not among the credited names, and he already has a prize, but his absence makes the story incomplete. Credit among the three is plausible but not clean.
assessment.maturity: Techniques are well confirmed by many groups, but the large-scale fundamental-physics results are still developing. Recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Absence of other key contributors (not on the supplied list) weakens the credit story.
Unclear whether the committee wants the method or specific measurement results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection of single NV centre spins in diamond and their coherent control produced a room-temperature solid-state qubit and a versatile nanoscale sensor for magnetic fields, temperature and strain. It is a clear case of an experimental discovery that created a field, with uses in biology, materials and quantum networks. The coherence times and sensitivities are quantifiable and impressive.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first optical detection and coherent manipulation of single NV spins (1997 and 2004), which is the core discovery. Lukin's group extended it to nanoscale sensing, quantum registers and entanglement, which is substantial but a second wave of work. A two-person prize for the founding experiments is cleanest, and a third slot for Lukin is conceivable.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced and extended the work, and commercial devices exist. The field is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Lukin should replace or join the experimental pair.
Overlap with the solid-state spin-photon interface candidate on Wrachtrup.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Production and quantum control of ultracold molecules enable precision tests of the electron electric dipole moment and ultracold chemistry, and give a route to new quantum simulators. Laser cooling of molecules and buffer-gas cooling are real experimental advances. The EDM limits are measurement-driven results with major consequences for beyond-Standard-Model physics.
assessment.attribution: DeMille and Doyle pioneered the key cooling and trapping methods and EDM experiments, while Ye contributed the KRb quantum-degenerate molecule work and precision spectroscopy. The group is credible but the credit spans several lines (association, direct cooling, EDM) and the boundaries are not obvious. Ye also appears on the optical lattice clock candidate, which would complicate a combined prize configuration.
assessment.maturity: The field is active and advances are recent; quantum-degenerate molecules and laser cooling are confirmed but still developing.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with multiple distinct approaches and other significant groups (for example Ni, Jin, Nägerl) not on the list.
Possibly premature relative to the older lattice clock and simulation topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for trapped-ion quantum computing and its experimental realization with entangling gates and algorithms demonstrated the viability of a leading quantum computing platform. The ion-trap qubit has the longest coherence times and the highest gate fidelities, which matters to someone who thinks in coherence and efficiency terms.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal. Blatt's group performed the first deterministic gate demonstrations and large-scale entangled-state work. Wineland (2012) and Monroe/Wineland's experimental gate work are not on the list and partly already recognized. The three names form a plausible theory and experiment configuration but the shared credit with the 2012 recipient is a concern.
assessment.maturity: The platform is mature and independent confirmation is strong, but practical computing is still unproven. Recognition could be seen as timely or still early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with other Cirac-Zoller candidates (Cirac and Zoller on several candidates).
Whether quantum computing results are mature enough for a physics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a conceptual invention with experimentally demonstrated implementations over fibre and satellites. Its impact beyond physics is clear, and it links to foundations through Bell-inequality tests recognized in 2022. The idea is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) and Ekert (E91, entanglement-based) are the standard credited trio, and the allocation is straightforward. Wiesner's early conjugate coding is a known historical complication outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental QKD is well replicated, but practical security depends on implementation and real-world deployment is limited. The 2022 prize partly covers the surrounding area.
uncertainties: Whether this is physics or computer science and cryptography.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement and quantum information science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a clear invention that opened the mid-infrared and terahertz ranges to compact semiconductor sources, and it is now used widely in trace-gas spectroscopy, sensing and metrology. As a measurement tool, it directly serves the sensing applications I value, and the demonstration of the first device in 1994 was unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: The Bell Labs team led by Capasso, with Faist as the first author, and Cho as the molecular-beam-epitaxy grower, is a natural configuration. Other team members (Sirtori, Hutchinson, Sivco) are not credited, and Kazarinov and Suris proposed the concept in 1971, which is a historical complication.
assessment.maturity: The device is mature, commercial and heavily replicated. Recognition is considered timely given the decades of use.
uncertainties: Whether the committee treats it as device engineering rather than physics discovery.
Credit questions about the earlier theoretical proposal and other Bell Labs co-inventors.
